facts.statement: The study aims to create optoelectronic synapses for vision systems that can sense specific light colors and update their signal strength smoothly.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Researchers adjusted the chemical structure of quasi-2D perovskite materials by changing a specific numerical parameter called the nominal n value.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: Adding the n = 2 phase to the material allowed it to absorb light up to 600 nm, creating distinct electrical responses to blue, green, and red light.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: A specific mixture with a nominal n value of 1.2 absorbed red light well while stopping harmful ion movement, resulting in very straight-line changes in electrical current.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The team built a mathematical model using the material's responses to light color, brightness, and time to estimate electrical warnings for blue light hazards and known damage thresholds.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The authors state that this method offers a way to combine color selection and linear signal processing at the material level for vision systems.
facts.subject: computational
